text:
maria: heads up — after the kernel-selector tweak last night I'm seeing a p50 regression (~+8%) on small prompt endpoints, and GPU KV cache hit-rate dropped hard :eyes:
kevin: ugh, saw that in dashboards too. metric spike lines up with batching heuristic change that favored larger micro-batches at 32-token window
sophie: larger micro-batches would increase transient memory + KV pressure. could cause earlier GPU->CPU crossover and more evictions
mar ia: exactly. my quick correlate: hit_rate_gpu=0.62 -> 0.47 around 02:13 deploy, total_evictions/sec +3.4x
perf-bot: nightly-regressions — service=text-gen-small p50 +7.9% p95 +11.8% | gpu_kv_hit:0.47 (-0.15) | cpu_kv_hit:0.68 (+0.06)
tim: I dumped KV allocator traces from a repro run. excerpt:
```
KV_ALLOC: gpu_pool_total=6.0GiB gpu_pool_free=512MiB slab_frag=18% free_slots=120k
EVICT: keys=3.4k avg_key_size=520B ttl_median=4.2m
BATCHER: target_mb=48 current_mb=64 micro_batch=32 -> chosen_kernel=fast_attn_v2
```
kevin: chosen_kernel=fast_attn_v2 changed cache layout? we made a small optimization that uses a different KV prefix for alignment to 128B which could change key fingerprinting
alex: that sounds like keying churn. if key fingerprints change, GPU cache sees low hit-rate even though logical prefixes are same :thinking:
sophie: also noticed frag increase on GPU slab after warmups. fragmentation + earlier evicts cause a feedback loop — warmup never finishes
mar ia: hypothesis: kernel selector change + batcher prefers bigger micro-batches -> different key normalization (alignment) -> effective key mismatch -> miss -> more GPU evictions -> p50 regression
infra-bot: replayed traffic test env-042 at 02:20 with current-prod vs canary: canary hit_rate_gpu=0.49 prod=0.63, mem_pressure_gpu +18%
tim: quick mitigation options:
- rollback kernel selector change (safe, will restore prior keying)
- adjust crossover threshold: delay GPU->CPU migration until gpu_free_ratio < 0.25
- increase GPU TTL for prefixes to allow warmup to finish (from 4m -> 10m)
kevin: rolling TTL might mask real leak but buys us time. I'd prefer a targeted rollback for the selector while we root-cause
alex: agreed. we should also add a unit smoke that validates stable key fingerprints across kernel variants. simple test: run a 1000-prefix sample through both kernels and compare normalized keys
sophie: created quick config patch for crossover policy, patch snippet:
```
{"gpu_cache_cutover_pct": 0.25, "gpu_prefix_ttl_ms": 600000, "kv_key_align": "legacy"}
```
maria: i pushed an infra-demo with ttl=10m and legacy key_align in a canary pool (pool-c17). early numbers look promising: gpu_hit up to 0.58 and p50 back down ~3%
perf-bot: canary-run: p50 -3.2% vs canary-base | gpu_kv_hit=0.58 (+0.11) | evictions/sec -42%
kevin: plan: rollback kernel-selector in canary, run the key-fingerprint smoke, then decide whether to reintroduce fast_attn_v2 with stable key normalization
tim: I'll open an RFC issue documenting the kernel-keying contract + add the smoke test to CI. tagging @sre for potential fallout windows
alex: action items:
- tim: RFC + CI smoke (ETA EOD)
- kevin: rollback in prod-canary + run full traffic compare (ETA 30m)
- sophie: monitor frag + evict rates and keep ttl patch ready (ETA 15m)
- maria: collect long-tail prefix entropy samples for last 24h
mar ia: thanks — I'll coordinate rollback and post updates here. if rollback looks good we'll cut a hotfix release to restore prior kernel behavior
infra-bot: incident-note created: "gpu-cpu-cache-crossover drift after kernel selector deploy" link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-7234
kevin: fyi we may also need a perf regression dashboard for kernel-selector changes explicitly (pinned metrics: gpu_hit_rate, evictions/sec, p50, mem_free_ratio)
alex: agree — let's not let keying be a first-class surprise again. also follow-up: quantify how batching heuristics change key entropy distribution
mar ia: ok i'll loop in research for entropy analysis. will report back in ~2 hours with sample stats
kevin: perfect. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
